description:
pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:141–146

    let current_issuer = path
        .last()
        .expect("path is never empty")
        .tbs_certificate
        .issuer
        .clone();

The comment 'path is never empty' is an invariant maintained by the caller (build_path always pushes target before the first call).  Using .expect() on an invariant that holds by construction is correct but results in a panic with a string message in release builds.

Idiomatic Rust for caller-maintained invariants is:
- debug_assert!(!path.is_empty(), "path is never empty") before the .last()
- Then use path.last().unwrap() or path.last_mut().unwrap() (or expect if preferred)

Alternatively, restructure dfs to accept the current cert directly rather than re-extracting it from the path:

    fn dfs(current: &Certificate, path: &mut Vec<Certificate>, ...) -> bool

This eliminates the invariant entirely and avoids the clone of current_issuer (which is cloned only to avoid a simultaneous immutable + mutable borrow — a separate issue). The restructured signature is cleaner and the invariant disappears.
title: dfs() uses bare .expect() on path.last() — prefer debug_assert
